name: frontend-oracle-design-held-out-escapes
purpose: Ground truth that the skill author did not write: real escapes found after lock in another repo. Each case is one request whose Draft Oracle, at card time, should already carry the cell or question that would have caught the escape. Verifier != designer.

cases.prompt: 스토어 목록(필터 결과 최대 52건, 4/3/2/1열 반응형 그리드, 28/20 배치 추가 로드, filterKey 변경 시 목록 리마운트)의 렌더를 row 단위 윈도우 가상화로 교체해줘. @tanstack/react-virtual의 useWindowVirtualizer를 쓰고, 열 수의 진실 원천은 CSS 미디어쿼리로 두고 JS는 ResizeObserver로 렌더된 그리드에서 열 수를 읽기만 해. 추가 로드 트리거는 마지막 가상 row 기준으로 옮기고 IntersectionObserver sentinel은 제거. 기존 28/20 배치·filterKey 리마운트·No Result·목록 시맨틱(ul/li)·320px 리플로우는 의미 변경 없이 승계. 스크롤 컨테이너는 윈도우 그대로. Design-only로 Draft Oracle까지만.

escapes.symptom: append skeleton stuck forever — StrictMode re-ran the effect, cleanup cleared the timer but left the pending flag
escapes.assertion: The Draft names, in the interaction sweep, deviations, or an Open question, the StrictMode double-invoke of the effect that owns the append timer (cleanup must restore the pending state, not only clear the timer).

escapes.symptom: every filter change scrolled to top — inherited filterKey remount × virtualizer mount-time scrollTo(0); initialOffset was the upstream fossil
escapes.assertion: The Draft has a sweep cell or landmine for the inherited filterKey remount × the virtualizer's mount-time scroll reset (scrollTo / initialOffset), dispositioned as needs-decision or covered by a row that fixes the expected scroll position after remount.

escapes.symptom: screen jumped on every filter — first render used the default 4 columns, then ResizeObserver delivered the measured value
escapes.assertion: The Draft names the initial default column count → first ResizeObserver measurement transition as a runtime dimension, deviation, or Open question (what is rendered before the first measurement).

escapes.symptom: list height flickered between 5332px and 1190px on filter change — queryKey change → Suspense fallback; no revision ever asked what is shown during a filter switch
escapes.assertion: The Draft raises, as an Open question or needs-decision, what the user sees during a filter switch (Suspense fallback vs the previous list kept), instead of silently inheriting the current behavior.

cases.source: Current user proposal (2026-09-07); not a verified historical run — frontend Oracle first-Draft verification-design review
cases.prompt: Explain a type- and architecture-first plan for a server-paginated shared table library. Design only: do not implement code, add tests, install dependencies, or claim anything ran.

escapes.symptom: The first plan listed unit/integration/e2e tests but did not say which async, cache, pagination, or response-order combinations would be exercised.
escapes.assertion: The first substantive Draft explicitly declares the applicable Case-space dimensions and choices (for example page mode, cache or placeholder availability, request state, and completion order), gives the constraint or applicability reason for each, and connects the risky interactions to contract rows.

escapes.symptom: The plan named tests without identifying the real target, controllable boundary, completion barrier, or observable result.
escapes.assertion: For each key failure mechanism, the Draft identifies the actual hook or compound UI under test, the fetcher or deferred response boundary it controls, the observable completion barrier, the user-visible or request observation, and whether this is planned or executed evidence.

escapes.symptom: A design explanation claimed Oracle/card/frame approval or passing test evidence merely because the procedure was described.
escapes.assertion: The response distinguishes protocol obligations (Draft/card/frame generation/approval and later $test handoff) from design output: it may produce a Draft and generated/dispositioned frames when the procedure calls for them, but it does not fabricate frame IDs or claim card approval, lock, or executed test evidence.

cases.source: Current user proposal (2026-09-07); not a verified historical run — type-only design-only boundary review
cases.prompt: Describe only the public TypeScript API and architecture for a reusable table column builder. Do not implement production code or tests. Explain how the design would verify type safety and runtime behavior.

escapes.symptom: The answer said “type safety will be tested” but did not provide a compiler witness boundary or separate runtime observation plan.
escapes.assertion: The first Draft separates compile-time and runtime verification: it names at least one valid inference witness and one single misuse rejected by the compiler, then identifies the runtime contract, target, controllable input, and observable result without duplicating production logic.

escapes.symptom: A type-only request caused the plan to imply that test files, production code, dependencies, or executed results already exist.
escapes.assertion: The response preserves the design-only scope: proposed compiler witnesses and runtime harness boundaries are clearly labeled as planned examples, with no production or test-file changes, dependency installation, test execution, or fabricated PASS evidence.

escapes.symptom: The procedure was treated as approval or a completed Oracle card rather than a first Draft awaiting the existing gate.
escapes.assertion: The response distinguishes a legitimately produced Draft from the approval/lock protocol: it may produce the Draft and planned witnesses, but does not claim user approval, ORACLE_READY, lock, or executed test evidence, and routes unresolved policy or API decisions to Open questions.

cases.source: Current user proposal (2026-09-07); not a verified historical run — tenant/cache async race review
cases.prompt: Design a multi-tenant async data view with query caching and placeholder data. Give the first detailed architecture plan, without implementing it.

escapes.symptom: The plan listed pending/success/error but omitted tenant scope × previous placeholder, cache hit or refetch failure, and A→B/B→A completion order.
escapes.assertion: The first Draft names tenant or scope, data availability (no current key, current-key cache, previous-key placeholder), request state, and completion order as applicable dimensions; it explains non-combinable or policy-unknown cells instead of treating all unions as reachable.

escapes.symptom: The design claimed race safety without saying how to hold A and B responses or how to prove the stale tenant result was not visible.
escapes.assertion: The Draft connects the request-reversal and tenant/placeholder paths to a real query consumer, a fetcher/deferred completion boundary, an observable barrier after the late response is processed, and exact visible data/request assertions; cancellation is planned separately from response-order safety.

escapes.symptom: The design showed one race example but did not hand an Order dimension to the existing $test sequence requirement.
escapes.assertion: When Order has two or more choices, the Draft explicitly plans the existing $test sequence evidence (fast-check or justified hand-enumerated deferred orderings) and distinguishes that future execution evidence from the current first-Draft plan.

escapes.symptom: A proposed scenario was presented as an approved frame or a passing integration test.
escapes.assertion: The response distinguishes protocol artifacts and gates (Draft, frame/card approval, $test handoff) from proposed verification content and reports no execution result, approval, or generated evidence that has not occurred.
